question: At what temperature in kelvin does liquid nitrogen boil at normal atmospheric pressure?
explainer: Liquid nitrogen boils at about 77 K, which is -196 °C: cold enough to shatter a rose, yet still some 75 degrees warmer than the LHC's superconducting magnets at 1.9 K.

question: Roughly how many lumens of light does a standard 60-watt incandescent light bulb give out?
source_title: Lumens and the Lighting Facts Label - U.S. Department of Energy
explainer: A classic 60 W bulb produces about 800 lumens, which is why LED bulbs sold as '60 W equivalent' are rated at 800 lumens while drawing only 8 to 10 watts.

question: According to the IAEA, how many nuclear power reactors were in operation worldwide at the end of 2024?
source_title: Nuclear Power Reactors in the World, 2025 Edition - IAEA
explainer: The IAEA counted 417 operating reactors with a combined capacity of about 377 GW at the end of 2024; counting Japanese units in long-term suspension pushes the figure to around 440.

question: How many main superconducting dipole magnets steer the beams around CERN's Large Hadron Collider ring?
source_title: Facts and figures about the LHC - CERN
explainer: The LHC uses 1,232 dipole magnets, each 15 metres long and weighing about 35 tonnes, chilled to 1.9 K so they can bend protons around the 27 km ring with an 8.3 tesla field.

question: How many gigawatt-hours of electricity did CERN consume in 2022?
explainer: CERN used about 1,215 GWh in 2022, roughly what a mid-sized European city uses in a year, with demand peaking near 200 MW while the accelerators run.

question: How many optical sensors (DOMs) are frozen into the Antarctic ice at the IceCube Neutrino Observatory?
explainer: IceCube's 5,160 digital optical modules hang on 86 strings between 1,450 and 2,450 metres deep, turning a cubic kilometre of South Pole ice into a neutrino telescope.

question: At what temperature in degrees Celsius does tungsten, the metal with the highest melting point, melt?
explainer: Tungsten melts at 3,422 °C, more than three times the melting point of gold (1,064 °C), which is why it was the filament of choice in incandescent bulbs for a century.

question: At what frequency, in megahertz, does a standard domestic microwave oven heat food?
explainer: Home microwave ovens run at 2,450 MHz, giving a wavelength of about 12 cm, in the same 2.4 GHz band shared by Wi-Fi and Bluetooth.

question: How many laps of the 27 km Large Hadron Collider ring does a proton complete every second?
source_title: Facts and figures about the LHC - CERN
explainer: Travelling at 99.9999991% of the speed of light, each proton circles the 26.7 km ring 11,245 times a second, covering a distance equal to seven and a half trips around the Earth.

question: How much will the ITER tokamak fusion machine being built in France weigh when complete, in tonnes?
explainer: The ITER tokamak will weigh 23,000 tonnes, about three times the mass of the Eiffel Tower, with its vacuum vessel alone accounting for roughly 5,000 tonnes.

question: How many tonnes of ultra-pure water fill the Super-Kamiokande neutrino detector in Japan?
explainer: Super-K's stainless-steel tank, 39 m across and 41 m tall, holds 50,000 tonnes of ultra-pure water watched by about 11,000 photomultiplier tubes, a kilometre underground in a mine.

question: What is the density of osmium, the densest naturally occurring element, in kilograms per cubic metre?
explainer: Osmium packs 22,590 kg into a cubic metre, more than 22 times the density of water and about twice that of lead; a one-litre bottle of it would weigh 22.6 kg, as much as a six-year-old child.

question: How much did the Hubble Space Telescope weigh at its launch in 1990, in kilograms?
explainer: Hubble weighed 11,110 kg at launch, roughly the mass of two adult African elephants, and gained about 1,000 kg of new instruments over five servicing missions.

question: How fast does Earth travel along its orbit around the Sun, in kilometres per hour?
explainer: Earth orbits the Sun at about 29.8 km/s, or 107,000 km/h, covering its own diameter every seven minutes and a full 940-million-kilometre loop each year.

question: How many tonnes of gold have been mined in all of human history, as of the end of 2025?
source_title: How much gold has been mined? - World Gold Council
explainer: Roughly 220,000 tonnes of gold have ever been mined, which would form a cube only about 22 metres on each side, and about two-thirds of it was dug up after 1950.

question: What is the voltage, in volts, of the world's highest-voltage power transmission line (China's Changji-Guquan link)?
explainer: The 1,100 kV DC line carries 12,000 MW over 3,300 km from Xinjiang to eastern China, nearly 5,000 times the 230 V of a European household socket.

question: What plasma temperature, in degrees Celsius, is the ITER fusion reactor designed to reach?
explainer: ITER aims for 150 million °C, about ten times hotter than the core of the Sun, because without the Sun's crushing gravity fusion needs far higher temperatures to work.

question: How many tonnes of crude steel were produced worldwide in 2024?
source_title: December 2024 crude steel production and 2024 global totals - worldsteel
explainer: The world made 1.88 billion tonnes of steel in 2024, over half of it in China, which is about 230 kg for every person on Earth.

question: What is the half-life of uranium-238, in years?
explainer: U-238's half-life of 4.47 billion years is almost exactly the age of the Earth, so about half of the uranium-238 present when the planet formed is still here.

question: How many pixels does the LSST camera at the Vera C. Rubin Observatory capture in a single image?
source_title: Largest camera ever built arrives at Rubin Observatory in Chile - NSF
explainer: The 3,200-megapixel LSST camera is the largest digital camera ever built; displaying one of its images at full resolution would take about 400 ultra-HD TV screens.

question: How many neutrinos from the Sun pass through each square centimetre of Earth every second?
explainer: About 65 billion solar neutrinos cross every square centimetre of your body each second, day and night, yet on average only one will interact with you in your whole lifetime.

question: How many joules of energy are released by the complete fission of 1 kilogram of uranium-235?
explainer: One kilogram of fully fissioned U-235 yields about 82 terajoules, roughly 23 million kWh, the same energy as burning around 2,700 tonnes of coal.
